en.name: Bonito flakes
en.summary: Bonito flakes are shavings of skipjack that has been simmered, smoked, dried and often fermented until it is as hard as wood. Unopened packs keep to the printed date in a cupboard; once opened, refrigerate for 1–2 months, or freeze for 6–12 months to hold the aroma.
en.pantry: An unopened pack keeps in a cool dry cupboard to the printed date, and no general number is given here because that date is the honest answer. What makes the flakes stable is how little moisture is left in them, so the enemy is air and humidity rather than bacteria. Keep packs away from the cooker and the kettle, out of the sun, and do not decant them into a jar that is not airtight. A pack that has gone soft or limp has taken up moisture and will go musty.
en.fridge: Once opened, press the air out of the bag, seal it and refrigerate: 1–2 months is a fair working figure, and it is about aroma rather than safety. Shavings lose their smell within weeks of meeting air, and what is left eventually tastes flat and cardboardy — that is the real end point, well before anything unsafe happens. Use a clean dry hand or tongs, never a wet spoon, and squeeze the bag flat each time. This figure is ordinary practice for an aroma-driven dried product, not a published number.
en.freezer: Freezing an opened bag holds the aroma far better than the cupboard or the fridge: 6–12 months at −18 °C (0 °F), again a quality figure rather than a published safety one. Double-bag it so it does not pick up freezer smells, and use it straight from frozen — there is so little water in the flakes that they do not clump, and dashi does not care that they were cold. A whole un-shaved block of katsuobushi is a different object and keeps far longer than shavings.
en.thawing: No thawing needed. Use the flakes straight from the freezer and reseal the bag immediately so condensation does not settle on them.
spoilage: Flakes that have gone soft, limp or slightly tacky instead of dry and brittle.
A musty or mouldy smell rather than a smoky-savoury one.
A flat, cardboard-like smell and no aroma when you open the bag.
Any visible mould, or a yellow-brown cast on flakes that should be pinkish-tan.
tips: Buy small packs; aroma is the whole point and it fades quickly.
Freeze the bag as soon as you open it.
Press all the air out before resealing.
Use tired flakes for a second-brew dashi or a furikake rather than throwing them out.

faq.q: How long do bonito flakes keep once opened?
faq.a: About 1–2 months refrigerated, or 6–12 months frozen. Both are quality figures — the flakes lose aroma long before they become unsafe.
Not before opening — a sealed pack keeps in a cool dry cupboard to its printed date. After opening, the fridge or freezer holds the aroma much better.
Yes, and it is the best way to keep an opened bag: 6–12 months at −18 °C. Use them straight from frozen.

faq.q: How can you tell if bonito flakes have gone off?
faq.a: They go soft or tacky, smell musty, or lose their smell altogether. Any visible mould means the bag goes.

zh.name: 柴魚片
zh.summary: 柴魚片是把鰹魚煮過、燻乾、乾燥並經常再經黴菌熟成到硬如木頭之後削出來的薄片。未開封放櫥櫃到標示日期；開封後冷藏 1～2 個月，或冷凍 6～12 個月以保住香氣。
zh.pantry: 未開封的包裝放在陰涼乾燥的櫥櫃裡到標示日期即可，這裡不另外給通用數字，因為那個日期就是誠實的答案。讓柴魚片穩定的是它極低的含水量，所以敵人是空氣和濕氣，不是細菌。包裝請遠離爐火與熱水瓶、避免陽光直射，也不要倒進不夠密封的罐子。整包摸起來變軟、沒了脆度，代表已經吸了水氣，接下來就會出現霉味。
zh.fridge: 開封後把袋內空氣擠出、封好冷藏：1～2 個月是合理的工作數字，而且講的是香氣而不是安全。削片一接觸空氣，香氣幾週內就開始跑掉，最後剩下的只是扁平的紙板味——那才是真正的終點，遠早於任何安全問題。用乾淨乾燥的手或夾子取，不要用濕湯匙，每次都把袋子壓平。這個數字是香氣型乾貨的一般做法，不是公告值。
zh.freezer: 開封後的整袋冷凍，保住香氣的效果遠勝櫥櫃或冷藏：−18 °C 下 6～12 個月，同樣是品質數字而非公告的安全值。請套兩層袋避免吸附冷凍庫氣味，用的時候直接從冷凍取——柴魚片含水極低，不會結塊，煮高湯也完全不在意它剛從冷凍出來。還沒削過的整塊柴魚是另一種東西，比削片耐放得多。
zh.thawing: 不需要解凍。直接從冷凍取用，並立刻把袋口封回去，避免水氣凝結在上面。
spoilage: 削片變軟、發蔫或略帶黏手，而不是乾脆易碎。
聞起來有霉味、陳味，而不是燻香與鮮味。
打開袋子幾乎沒有香氣，只剩紙板味。
看得到霉，或本該是粉褐色的削片轉為黃褐色。
tips: 買小包；香氣就是它的全部，而且散得很快。
封口前把空氣全部擠出來。
香氣走掉的柴魚片拿去煮二番高湯或做香鬆，不要直接丟。

faq.q: 柴魚片開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 冷藏約 1～2 個月，冷凍約 6～12 個月。兩者都是品質數字——香氣會遠早於安全問題先消失。
開封前不用，密封包放陰涼乾燥櫥櫃到標示日期即可。開封後放冷藏或冷凍，香氣保存好得多。
可以，而且是開封後最好的保存方式：−18 °C 下 6～12 個月，直接從冷凍取用。

faq.q: 怎麼判斷柴魚片壞掉了？
faq.a: 變軟、發黏、有霉味，或完全沒有香氣。看得到霉就整袋丟棄。
